releaseNotes: NChat 1.0.46 — the chat list finally describes the message it is quoting. Every row is derived from the message itself: a voice note shows its length, a photo or clip shows its caption, a document its file name, and a group says who spoke ('Nasir: …', 'You: …') instead of pretending everything is one anonymous voice. Delete or edit a message and the row follows; a send that failed shows a red 'not sent' mark instead of a tick that lied. Replies are real now: the quoted message's id travels with the send as reply_to, so a reply arrives as a reply on the other phone (and from the web app), with the quoted author and text resolved locally — including for voice notes and photos, which quote as 'Voice message (0:04)' rather than an empty strip. Forwarding copies the message instead of its description: a forwarded photo is a photo, a forwarded voice note plays. Deleting is honest in both directions — a message deleted for everyone keeps its slot as 'This message was deleted' on every device, a delete the server refuses (a group message older than an hour) is put back with the reason, deleting a message that is still queued cancels it instead of letting the next reconnect deliver it, and a group message deleted 'for me' no longer reappears on the next refresh. Voice notes got a scrubber: touch or drag the waveform to jump anywhere in the clip, the play button answers on the tap instead of after the first buffer, and a tap-then-pause while it is still loading stays paused. Privacy settings are remembered on the device, so the Privacy screen tells the truth on an offline launch.
